_readme: FIAT ART 76 (9 Nov; the ARPG slice, slice/README.md): the slice's own top-down sprites and tiles, 37 jobs, all at $0.08 (every canvas under 65k px); about $2.96, $3.85 with a 30% reroll budget.

20 figures (runner, gang1..3, hard x aim, fire, reload, down; 64x64, from directly above, facing +x) and 17 tiles and props (64 px canvas = one 32 px tile on screen), out to slice/art/pl/<name>.png. Style image art/map/land.png (the game's own top-down painting); the Kenney figures as a view-only reference. Nothing on disk is overwritten.
Wiring after art.done: slice/art.gd reads slice/art/pl/ by name (art76_names.md). ++ --parallel 3.
Regenerate with python3 tools/make_art76_manifest.py; check with python3 tools/art_lint.py tools/pixellab_art76_manifest.json.

jobs.description: Top-down pixel-art game character sprite seen from directly above, looking straight down onto the top of his head and shoulders: a lean poacher in a worn olive waxed jacket and a brown tweed flat cap, the cap's top and peak the nearest thing to the eye, standing, aiming: both arms forward to the right holding a long bolt-action hunting rifle with a dark wooden stock and a scope pointing straight to the right. He faces right: head in the centre, shoulders running up and down the frame, the gun pointing to the right. Not a side view, not in profile, not from the front, no legs seen from the side. One gun only, held by exactly two hands. The figure small and centred, clear of every edge. Only the palette, light and painting style of the style image, not its view or its subject; only the view from directly above of the reference image, not its colours or its flat style. Muted, grim, cold palette, worn and dirty clothes, painterly pixel shading. The figure alone on a transparent background: no floor, ground, shadow, shadow disc or setting around it. No text, no lettering, no logos.
jobs._where: slice figure runner, aim (art.gd; faces +x, about 30 px on screen)
